I've been fighting this stupid trackpad for a month now.

I've written a script using xinput and a hotkey to turn it off, but it turns off all connected mice. Even my nice wireless USB mouse.

I've tried several dark incantations found on various corners of the web to try to force xorg to recognize my touchpad as a synaptics device to no avail.

I'm looking for:

  • a way to disable /dev/mouse0 from making it to the mux, effectively disabling the trackpad
  • a way to force xorg into recognizing the trackpad as a synaptics device so I can disable it that way

Or some other way I haven't thought of to disable this one, annoying, pointing device.

FIXT

Add /etc/X11/xorg.conf.d/mouse.conf with the following:

Section "ServerFlags" 
 Option "AutoAddDevices" "No"
EndSection
Section "InputDevice"
 Identifier "logitech"
 Driver "mouse"
 Option "Device" "/dev/wsmouse1"
EndSection

This results in the trackpad not working at all, which is what I wanted. I can always use the USB mouse when I need to point and click at stuff.
